title: Milo and the Moon Pebble
markdown:
Once upon a time, way up in the sparkly whispery Silverpine Peaks, lived a young wizard named Milo Bells. His hat was a teeny bit too pointy, so it wobbled when he walked. His eyes were bright as two little shooting stars. The peaks felt like a giant green huggable blanket, soft and quiet and oh-so-cozy, and Milo Bells loved them with his whole wobbly hat.

Every single day, Milo Bells went for a walk. Swish, swish, swish went his robe, a happy little whisper through the tall pines. He practised spells that went, “Wiggle-wobble, make it so,” and “Sparkle-dazzle, here you go.” He liked the quiet. He liked the pine-needle hush. Still, just a little sometimes, he wished there was someone to say “Wow” when a spell sat up and behaved.

Until one day, as the sky put on its sleepy pink and purple pajamas, Milo Bells heard a funny noise. Not a hoot. Not a squirrel rustle. Huff. Puff. GRRRUNT.

“Hmm,” thought Milo Bells, and his pointy hat gave a little wobble of curiosity. “That sounds like someone trying very hard to do something super-duper important.”

Because of that, Milo Bells tiptoed toward the grunt. And there, wiggling a moss-green tail with all its might, was a round fluffy creature. Fur as soft as moss on the oldest trees. Ears twitching like tiny feelers. It was trying to push a pebble. But this pebble was as big as a little fluffy cloud that had decided to land in the woods. The creature wiggled its bottom. It pushed with tiny paws. Huff, puff, grunt. The cloud-pebble would not budge. It was like trying to push a sleepy mountain.

“Oh, hello there,” Milo Bells whispered, as soft as dandelion fluff, because he did not want to startle anyone so busy being brave.

The creature looked up with honey-coloured eyes and made a humming noise, like a tiny bumblebee at a flower. Milo Bells giggled.

“That pebble is a bit of a big one for you, isn’t it?”

He looked closer. It was not really a pebble. It looked like a little piece of the moon that had tumbled down, sparkling with the softest silver dust.

Because of that, Milo Bells decided he had to help. He knew a spell. He wiggled his fingers into little sparkly shapes.

“Little pebble, light as a feather, float and fly now, altogether.”

Nothing happened. The cloud-pebble stayed exactly where it was, looking very solid indeed.

“Oh dear,” Milo Bells sighed, and his pointy hat drooped like a wilting daisy. “That spell is for much smaller things, I suppose.”

Just then a soft warm light bobbed through the trees. Glimmerwick, the friendly goblin lantern-keeper, nose wiggling, lantern like a tiny captured sunbeam.

“Hello, Milo Bells,” he chirped, voice like happy little bells. “What’s all this grunting and puffing about?”

Milo Bells explained: the moss-furred creature, the very big cloud-pebble. Glimmerwick peered, nose even faster.

“My, oh my. That’s a mighty fine piece of the sky. And you, little one, you have the strength of a hundred happy hedgehogs all rolled into one.”

Because of that, Glimmerwick had an idea.

“You see, Milo Bells, sometimes the best magic isn’t a spell that goes poof. This little friend loves to carry things. Maybe it needs a friend to push with it. And you have strong hands. That’s a sort of magic too.”

So Milo Bells and Glimmerwick stood on one side of the giant cloud-pebble. The little moss-furred creature, whom Milo Bells had already decided was perfect for the name Flibbert, because he looked as if he might flibbert and flutter if he were not so busy being strong, stood on the other.

“Okay, Flibbert. On the count of three, we push together. One… two… three.”

With a gentle happy rumble, the cloud-pebble began to slide. Milo Bells pushed. His wizard boots dug into the soft ground. Flibbert grunted with pure determination. Glimmerwick’s lantern shone as brightly as it could, a little guiding star. The earth squished. The air smelled of pine needles and moonlight dust. The cloud-pebble rolled along, not too fast, not too slow, just perfectly right.

Until finally they arrived at a little clearing bathed in soft silvery moonlight. Flibbert let out a jiggly hum, a tune like tiny dancing stars, and nudged the cloud-pebble with a little nose, as if to say, this is the perfect spot for you.

Milo Bells’s heart felt as warm as a mug of sweet cocoa, though the cocoa was still waiting at home. He looked at Flibbert. Flibbert looked back.

“I think Flibbert was trying to bring it somewhere really special,” Milo Bells whispered.

Glimmerwick’s nose wiggled. He did not make a speech about teamwork being the most wonderful magic. He only held the lantern steady while Flibbert gave the moon-piece one last proud nudge.

Ever since then, Milo Bells’s evening walks in the Silverpine Peaks were never lonely. Flibbert would often be waiting, sometimes nudging a shiny fallen leaf, sometimes a smooth round acorn, and Milo Bells was always happy to help, his pointy hat wobbling with a smile. On quiet evenings, if you listened very closely, you could hear a soft hum and a little giggle on the breeze. The pines kept the sound, the way they kept the silver dust, and Milo Bells’s robe went swish, swish, swish, all the way home.
characters: Milo Bells (young wizard), Flibbert (moss-furred creature), Glimmerwick (goblin lantern-keeper)
author: StoryGen Community
